#28 Is it possible to install the software from the nlab repo on a local machine, create a database and import the data from the nlab-content repos ?
As a not-too-experienced-user I am having a hard time getting the nlab software to run for several ruby-related reasons, but now, when starting ./instiki daemon, it seems like it is looking for some database.

If some tech member could find the time and talk about how to properly set up the nlab software and a db and connect those, I would really appreciate it. Furthermore, as I understand it, the content repos are meant as a backup so there should be a way to import them into a db (?).

In a broader context, I thought it would be nice to have a living offline copy of the nlab on a smartphone. It seems atleast theoretically possible because you can run ruby and even ruby on rails environments on Android AFAIK.
Then just use a WebView to connect to the locally running software like a browser would.
subject: Query at HowTo on downloading the nLab
